clusters.text: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake has hit a mountainous region in Tibet, killing at least 16 people and injuring dozens, according to Chinese state media. The centre of the quake hit Baqên County in the Nagqu region on Thursday night, Xinhua reported, citing the local emergency management bureau. The county - located in what China calls the Tibet Autonomous Region after annexing it in the 1950s - is 400km (250 miles) north-east of the region's capital, Lhasa. Authorities have declared the incident an emergency and deployed rescue teams to the affected area, where 65 others have been injured, including 11 people with severe injuries. The electricity supply has been cut off and 339 homes have collapsed in the affected region, though by Friday morning there were reports of power restored in some areas. Local media said more than 12,400 people had been relocated following the earthquake. Rockfall has forced roads in the region to close, making it more difficult for crews to reach impacted high-altitude areas. The US Geological Survey (USGS) has recorded seven tremors close to the epicentre, all of which are located in the mountainous region. The largest tremor was recorded at 5.2 magnitude at a depth of 10km. Shallow earthquakes and tremors closer to the Earth's surface are more damaging than deep quakes. Several survivors of the earthquake have told local media about their harrowing escape. Nagqu resident Yixi Cuomu told Tibet Daily that she was asleep in her bed when her house started shaking violently. Realising it was an earthquake, she headed outside barefoot, her "legs trembling uncontrollably" as she descended the staircase in her home. Another eyewitness said the shaking was so violent "that in that moment I felt as if several hundred yaks were running past us". Residents chose to spend the night outdoors in subzero temperatures, seeking shelter in tents or their cars, as they feared aftershocks could trap them in their homes, according to the news outlet. Chinese state media reported on Friday morning that more than 400 aftershocks had been registered since the quake occurred. China's Premier Li Qiang has called for "urgent efforts" to organise rescue operations and medical treatment for the injured, and relocate and resettle affected residents appropriately, according to state media. clusters.text: Isack Hadjar has argued that Red Bull did not have the fastest car at the Singapore Grand Prix, and believes his team-mate Max Verstappen would have won by a bigger margin had he been driving a Ferrari. Verstappen heads into this weekend's United States Grand Prix on the back of two consecutive wins at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and the Singapore Grand Prix. The Dutchman dominated the race weekend at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, claiming pole position for both the sprint race and grand prix, and winning both races. But while speaking in the drivers' press conference in Austin, Hadjar played down suggestions the Milton Keynes outfit now has the fastest car on the grid. "No, because I think the car is still very hard to drive. In Malaysia, it was dominant, but I don't think in Singapore it was the fastest car." When pressed on why, given the four-time champion had won by 7.3 seconds over second-placed Charles Leclerc, Hadjar added: "That’s what I believe. I think if you put Max in the Ferrari, he would have won the race with more margin. So that’s my opinion." Hadjar said Verstappen made the most of every advantage he had, rather than relying on the pace of his Red Bull machinery. Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Team Principal, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images "He qualified on pole by half a tenth. Ferrari didn’t have new tyres in the race, not on the soft, so this has an effect as well," the French-Algerian driver explained. "He put all the chances on his side, he made the difference in Q3 and that was enough." Interestingly, McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who joined Hadjar in the press conference, said that Red Bull's upgrades introduced at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix were "very strong" and that it had become "the most consistently quick car" over the last few races. With six rounds remaining, Red Bull sits fourth in the constructors' championship, seven points behind McLaren in third. Verstappen is also fourth in the drivers' standings with 221 points, closing in on Lewis Hamilton in third on 229 points, and Hadjar is eighth with 97 points.

The blackbuck population at Chand Khamariya Blackbuck Sanctuary in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, has increased from 508 in 2022 to 604, according to the latest census by the forest department. Officials have attributed the rise to habitat improvement, better access to drinking water and efforts to reduce human interference in the protected area. The census was conducted between August and September by the forest department in collaboration with experts from Acharya Narendra Dev University of Agriculture and Technology in Ayodhya. The findings offer an encouraging picture of blackbuck conservation in the trans-Yamuna region, where the animals frequently move beyond the sanctuary's boundaries into neighbouring villages. “This is not only a positive indicator for wildlife conservation but also demonstrates that initiatives launched by the Yogi Adityanath government to protect wildlife and mitigate human-wildlife conflict are delivering results on the ground,” said Arvind Kumar, divisional forest officer (Prayagraj). The latest survey recorded 604 blackbucks across different age and sex groups, providing officials with a clearer picture of the population's composition. The count included 344 adult females, 92 adult males, 72 sub-adult females, 45 sub-adult males and 51 fawns. Researchers also assessed indicators such as the sex ratio and the number of young animals to help evaluate the population's long-term prospects. Yashmita Naveen, assistant professor in the university's department of agroforestry, said the sanctuary was divided into several sectors for the exercise. The census involved preliminary surveys, transect surveys, pilot surveys and waterhole counts. The highest concentration was recorded near Itwa Kala village, which accounted for 122 blackbucks. Mahuli Kala followed with 121, while Kihuni Kala recorded 114. The remaining animals were distributed across Purwa, Chand Khamariya, Baijala Pahadi and Majra Pahadi. The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), Allahabad Bench, by an order dated October 7, 2026, dismissed his Original Application, holding that a one-word WhatsApp reply of “OK” cannot by itself be treated as conclusive proof that the competent authority sanctioned his leave [Priya Ranjan Kumar v. clusters.text: The Ranchi Municipal Corporation removed around 14 unauthorised structures near Karbala Chowk on the Bahubazar route on Thursday, October 22, in a drive aimed at clearing public land, easing traffic congestion and restoring access along the road in Ward 16. The demolished structures included temporary shops, kiosks and unauthorised meat stalls built on government land and along road margins. RMC officials also removed temporary sheds, a dilapidated boundary wall and other structures that the civic body said were obstructing vehicular movement on the busy stretch. According to an RMC statement, the encroachments had contributed to traffic congestion and made it difficult for vehicles to move through the area. The removal of the boundary wall also improved access to a public toilet located near the site, the corporation said. The action followed a public notice issued by the civic body directing occupants to vacate the government land within three days. RMC officials said the demolition was carried out after the structures remained in place beyond the notice period. The sequence reflects the corporation’s stated enforcement process of issuing a direction before taking action against structures occupying public land or obstructing roads. The drive covered commercial activity on and beside the road, including temporary vending and meat stalls. RMC warned that unauthorised vending, fruit and vegetable markets and other commercial activities would not be permitted on the stretch without approval from the competent authority. The corporation said people occupying public land or creating traffic obstructions would face action under the relevant rules. Its statement also said similar anti-encroachment drives would continue across Ranchi to keep roads accessible, reduce bottlenecks and improve traffic management. The action near Karbala Chowk highlights the operational challenge faced by civic authorities when temporary commercial activity expands into road margins and public land. In this case, the municipal corporation linked the enforcement drive to both traffic movement and access to a public facility. Further action across the city will depend on the corporation’s continuing inspections and enforcement of its notices.
